To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BRCA1 and the BRCA2 genes have been found to have a high mutation rate in human sporadic cancers of the breast.
the BRCA1 and 2 genes have been identified as the major genes involved in hereditary breast and ovarian cancers.
BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 gene mutation was identified in 7.5% (5/66) of the sporadic breast cancers, which is similar to the mutation frequency of BRCA1/2 genes reported in other countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of BRCA1, BRCA2 gene mutation and its clinical significance.
the study of the mutations of BRCA1 gene and BRCA2 in human sporadic cancers.
the analysis of the frequency and distribution of BRCA1/2 gene mutations in sporadic breast cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 gene mutation is not the major cause of sporadic breast cancer in Chinese Han women, but it is a significant factor in familial breast cancer.
BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations are found in 5-10% of all sporadic breast cancer patients.
the BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations were detected in 3.6% of all breast cancer patients, 5.9% of all breast cancers and 9.2% of all breast carcinomas with a family history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BRCA1/BRCA2 gene mutations have been found in human sporadic cancers and that the mutations of BRCA1/2 genes are associated with breast cancer.
the BRCA1 and the BRCA2 genes play a significant role in breast carcinogenesis and that the mutations are more prevalent in the sporadic breast cancer patients than in the general population.
BRCA1 and 2 gene mutations are rare in sporadic breast cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations were found in about 10% of sporadic breast cancers.
the BRCA2 gene is a major susceptibility gene for breast and ovarian cancer in the Ashkenazi Jewish population.

BRCA1 and 2 mutations in breast cancer are not rare, and that they are not confined to families with a strong history of breast cancer, but rather are found in the general population. 2002 Jul;9(4):275-81. doi: 10.1097/00001702-200207000-00001.
